answers.docs.gaps:
- Wrong: `AppFailure`. Quoted in the friction answer — the docs give it an
  import path, a constructor signature and two worked examples, and the symbol
  is not in standout 9.0.0 under any path I could reach.
  `docs/topics/stability.md` even lists it as contract ("that is `AppFailure`,
  and `ExternalFailure` for a status another operation declared").

- Missing: whether owner-declared failures work from a *passthrough* handler.
  `docs/topics/passthrough.md` says only "the `anyhow::Error` becomes the
  command's failure", and `docs/topics/error-handling.md` frames both failure
  types as reached "through the same `HandlerResult` seam" — which passthrough
  does not use. It does work (`gitlike cat-object nosuch` exits 3 with the
  exact stderr line, `gitlike config get log.limit` exits 1 silently), but I
  found that out by running it, not by reading it.

- Missing: `ExitStatus`'s accessor. `docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md` shows
  `assert_eq!(result.exit_status(), Some(ExitStatus::SUCCESS))` but never says
  how a printing caller turns that into a process status. `.code()` returning
  `u8` was a guess that compiled.

- Missing: whether `App::get_matches_from` / `App::run_with` take `&self`.
  Both do, so one `App` can be parsed against and then run; the docs' examples
  never show both on the same value, and I had `let mut app` until the
  unused-`mut` warning told me otherwise.

- Missing: paging for command output, covered in the friction answer.
  `docs/topics/output-modes.md` mentions `myapp list | less` only as an example
  of color detection, never as something the framework can drive.
answers.friction:
a) `AppFailure` does not exist. `docs/topics/error-handling.md` says:

    use standout::cli::{AppFailure, HandlerResult};
    ...
    return Err(AppFailure::new(1, "ghlike: repository not found: demo/gamma\n")?.into());

and `docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md` repeats it. The build says:

    error[E0432]: unresolved import `standout::cli::AppFailure`
      --> src/plumbing.rs:11:21
       |
    11 | use standout::cli::{AppFailure, CommandContext};
       |                     ^^^^^^^^^^ no `AppFailure` in `cli`

`standout::AppFailure` and `standout_dispatch::AppFailure` fail the same way,
and rustc offers no similar-name suggestion, so nothing close to that spelling
is exported. `ExternalFailure` *is* there — rustc suggested it when I misspelled
it — so I used that instead. See the workarounds answer.

b) No paging seam for command output. The only paging in `docs/` is
`docs/topics/topics-system.md` ("For long topics, the `--page` flag displays
content through a pager") and `docs/topics/standout-help.md` ("paging is a
terminal side effect and only a *printing* entry point may perform it"). Since
SPEC.md requires porcelain commands to page, and `run()` owns the final write,
I had to move to `run_with` and re-implement the process edge. That is a
documented capture path, but it means re-deriving behavior `run()` gets for
free (the trailing newline, the stderr split, the exit status).

c) Getting the trailing newline right needed care.
`docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md#the-trailing-newline-contract` says
the engine eats one final newline and "`App::run` writes a handled command's
text with `writeln!`". A naive `{% for %}` loop whose body ends in a newline
therefore renders with a trailing newline *and* gets one appended, producing a
blank last line. I wrote the loop's separator as
`{% if not loop.last %}<newline>{% endif %}` so the rendered string ends
without a newline, matching what `writeln!` expects.

d) Writing an "unstyled" theme is not obvious. `docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md`
says an undefined tag in `Term` mode gets a marker: "Unknown tags get a `?`
marker: `[unknown?]text[/unknown?]`". So `mono` could not simply omit the
styles — it has to define every tag with a declaration that resolves to no
attributes. I used `opacity: 1` (the doc only documents `opacity: 0.5` as
dim) and verified with `GITLIKE_THEME=mono gitlike log --output term` that the
bytes are plain, with no ANSI and no `?` markers.

answers.summary:
`gitlike`, complete and building clean (`cargo build`, no warnings from my
code), with every command in SPEC.md verified by running the binary.

Structure in `app/src/`:

- `repo.rs` — the frozen three-commit / two-branch state, as consts.
- `config.rs` — the two config keys, resolved from the nearest `.gitlike.toml`
  walking up from the cwd, then `$GITLIKE_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` (else
  `$HOME/.config/gitlike/config.toml`). Precedence is per key: the repo file
  wins for the keys it sets, the user file fills the rest. Both TOML spellings
  (`log.limit = 2` and `[log] limit = 2`) work, because the toml crate
  normalizes dotted keys.
- `cli.rs` — clap derive plus `#[derive(Dispatch)]`. `log` and `status` are
  `#[dispatch(pure)]`; the plumbing variants are `#[dispatch(skip)]`.
- `handlers.rs` — the two porcelain `#[handler]` adapters returning view data.
- `templates/log.jinja`, `templates/status.jinja`, `styles/default.css`,
  `styles/mono.css`.
- `plumbing.rs` — `ref-list`, `cat-object` and `config get`, registered with
  `command_passthrough`. That was the deliberate design choice for the
  stability contract: a passthrough handler writes its own bytes and, per
  `docs/topics/passthrough.md`, `--output` has no way to reach it, so the
  plumbing bytes are identical under every theme, every `--output` mode and
  terminal or pipe. I verified that as a matrix (8 output modes × 5
  environments for `ref-list`, 8 modes for `cat-object`) — all byte-identical.
- `pager.rs` — paging, which the framework does not provide for command output
  (only for help/topics). Porcelain pages when stdout is a terminal, the
  invocation did not pass `--no-pager`, and `GITLIKE_PAGER` (else `PAGER`)
  names a non-blank command, which is run through `sh -c`.
- `main.rs` — `App::builder()` wiring plus `run_with`, because the process edge
  had to be mine to page: `run()` performs the final write itself. `main` does
  what `run()` documents — one trailing newline via `writeln!`, diagnostics to
  stderr, the framework's own exit status — and routes porcelain text through
  the pager plan instead of straight to stdout.

Theme selection reads `GITLIKE_THEME` at build time and feeds
`.default_theme("mono"|"default")`. `NO_COLOR` and pipe-vs-terminal are the
framework's `auto` mode doing its documented job; I add nothing there.

Exit codes verified: 0 success, 1 `config get` on an unset key (silent on both
streams), 2 unknown command / unknown flag / `--limit 0` / missing argument,
3 unknown object hash (with `gitlike: no such object: <hash>` on stderr).
answers.workarounds:
- `src/plumbing.rs` uses `ExternalFailure` where the docs' blessed seam is
  `AppFailure`. Semantically `ExternalFailure` is documented for "relaying a
  verdict" another executable reached, which `gitlike` is not doing; I use it
  purely because it is the surviving type with the required shape (nonzero
  status + verbatim stderr payload, no framing). A comment above the import
  says so. If `AppFailure` reappears, swapping the two names is the whole fix.

- `src/main.rs` uses `run_with` rather than the blessed `run`, and
  reimplements the final write, so that porcelain can be paged. The cost is
  that framework warnings are dropped: `run()` flushes them to stderr, and
  capture runs drain them instead. `gitlike` produces none, but I do not
  forward `result.warnings()`, so a future one would be silent.

- `src/pager.rs` parses the command line twice — once via
  `app.get_matches_from(...)` to learn whether the invocation is porcelain and
  whether `--no-pager` was passed, then again inside `run_with`. Paging has to
  be decided before dispatch and there is no hook that reports the resolved
  command to the caller ahead of the run.

- The pager is run through `sh -c`, so `PAGER="less -R"` works. A pager
  command that does not exist is a successfully-spawned shell that then fails,
  which means that invocation's output is lost (as it is with git). Only a
  shell that will not start at all falls back to stdout.

- Malformed config is treated as absent rather than as an error: an
  unparseable `.gitlike.toml`, a non-integer `log.limit`, or a non-positive
  one all resolve to "unset". SPEC.md's exit-code table enumerates 0/1/2/3 and
  has no status for a bad config file, so I kept the tool inside that set
  rather than inventing one.
